title: i18n: a native-speaker read of the agent-written security advisory sentences before the console renders them (ar, ja, ko, zh-Hant first)
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgU7jN46DmQ6XFvz28s

Filing gate: ④ a sub-card of tracking #32654. Layer 3 (#32657, the console renders `userMessage`) should be `Blocked-by:` this card, at least for the four locales named below.
Business reason: #32655 (PR #32790) ships non-English user sentences for 7 security-posture advisory rules in 10 locales: 70 entries, of which the field-mask entry has three arms per locale (which half of the restriction is inert) and the owner-policy entry three remedy variants. An agent wrote all of them, borrowing terms from the console packs (`ui/packages/i18n`), and no native speaker has read them. Once #32656 composes them and #32657 renders them, they become the first platform-composed text a non-English admin reads about their permission sets. A wrong term in a security sentence, such as the setting's name or what the fix grants, sends the admin to the wrong setting or makes them distrust the advice. The rule ids stay the same, so a correction is a data-only PR.
Reader who acts: the `domain:ui` / `area:i18n` seat arranges the read. A native read means a human reader per locale: an agent can check the terms against the console packs but cannot sign off a native read. If the fleet has no such reader, this card needs the maintainer's call on who reads it, or on whether to ship on the English-reviewed terms alone.
Dedupe words: `native review`, `security posture user text`, `validate-security-posture.user-text`, `agent-written translation`.

Back-link: #32655 · #32657 · parent #32654 · ⛔ Not a claim. Grading is triage's.

## What to read

`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.user-text.ts`: one sentence per rule id per locale. The `BYPASS_LABEL` table holds each locale's label for View All Records and Modify All Records.

| Rule id | What the sentence tells the admin |
|---|---|
| `security-private-no-readscope` | holders of the set see only the records of a private object that they own or that are shared with them; give the set a read scope or widen sharing |
| `security-master-detail-ungranted` | no permission set grants a detail object, so everyone but administrators is refused it |
| `security-book-audience-unknown-set` | a book is restricted to a permission set that is not defined, so no one can open it |
| `security-superuser-field-mask-inert` | hiding a field, making it read-only, or both, has no effect because the set holds View All / Modify All Records on the object (three arms, by the `inert` param) |
| `security-controlled-by-parent-master-reference-hidden` | the set hides the link to the master record, so a refused holder is not told which master the change needs |
| `security-update-policy-no-check` | an update policy sets no check condition, so an update may save rows the default ownership rule allows. Contract review nit N2 (record 6835490406): the sentence prescribes adding a check condition without the side effect the rule's `hint` states (a creator who is not the owner loses update unless the check admits them); the reader decides whether every locale should carry that caveat |
| `security-controlled-by-parent-owner-policy-without-opt-in` | an update policy on an object that takes edit access from its master can only narrow who edits it (three remedy variants) |

Locales: `zh-Hans`, `zh-Hant`, `ja`, `ko`, `ar`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `pt-BR`, `ru`. **Read `ar`, `ja`, `ko` and `zh-Hant` first.** The #32655 developer reported that those console packs had the least existing wording to borrow terms from (report 6823397904).

## Done when

Each locale has a named reader's sign-off, or a data-only PR that edits that locale's sentences in the catalog. The rule ids, params and pins stay the same. Each edited sentence must still pass `finding-user-text.test.ts`, which requires that no sentence is the English stand-in.

## Not in scope

The 67 advisory rules that do not have sentences yet (tracking card #32835). Their PRs name their own agent-written sentences for the same kind of read.
